summary: André Wedemeyer was a scholar of Sinology, Japanology, and linguistics. He completed his doctoral studies under August Conrady and held a post at the University of Leipzig from circa 1914 to 1945.

Andy Rotman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and completed his dissertation at the University of Chicago under Sheldon Pollock and Steven Collins, later serving at Smith College.

Angela Falco Howard specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history and archaeology. She completed her doctoral dissertation at New York University under Alexander C. Soper and held a professorship at Rutgers University attested in 2005.
Angela Manderscheid is a scholar in Tibetology and other fields. She held posts at the Free University of Berlin and at the University of Oulu, where she was attested as a researcher in 1998.

Angela Sumegi is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who earned her Ph.D. at the University of Ottawa and studied under Nalini Devdas. She served as an assistant professor at Carleton University, attested in 2008.

Angela Zito is a scholar in religious studies and Sinology who earned her Ph.D. from the University of Chicago in 1989. Around 2000, she served as an associate professor of anthropology and religious studies at New York University.

Philosopher Angelika Krebs completed her PhD at Goethe University Frankfurt under Bernard Williams. She served as an assistant professor in Frankfurt (1993–2001) and held the Lehrstuhl für Praktische Philosophie at the University of Basel in 2001.

Angelika Malinar is an Indology and religious studies scholar who completed her PhD and Habilitation at the University of Tübingen. She served at SOAS University of London (circa 2000–2007) and became an associate professor at the University of Zurich in 2009.

Angelo Brelich was a religious studies and history and archaeology scholar. He studied at Erzsébet University from circa 1932 to 1937 and held a post at the University of Rome from circa 1958 to 1977.

Angelo De Gubernatis was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Universities of Turin and Berlin. He served as professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at Florence (1863–1891) and professor at the University of Rome in 1890.

Anil Vidyalankar is a scholar of linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya, Columbia University, and the University of Delhi, and served as director of Sandhaan, which he founded in 1988.

Ankur Barua is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned an MBuddStud from the University of Hong Kong in 2009, having previously studied at Manipal Academy and Sikkim Manipal. He held a post at the University of Delhi in 2012.

Ann Appleby Hazlewood is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned a Master of Arts at the Australian National University, attested in 1983, under the supervision of Tissa Rajapatirana and Luise Hercus.
Ann Gleig is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned her Doctor of Philosophy at Rice University under the supervision of Jeffrey J. Kripal.

Ann Grodzins Gold is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She earned her degrees, including a PhD, at the University of Chicago and held faculty posts at Cornell University (circa 1988–1993) and Syracuse University (circa 1993–2021).

Ann Heirman is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. She worked for the National Fund for Scientific Research (1995–2009) and served as a professor and head of the Centre for Buddhist Studies at Ghent University.

Ann Laura Stoler is a historian and anthropologist who studied at Barnard College and Columbia University. She taught at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and the University of Michigan before chairing the anthropology department at The New School in 2004.

Anna Aurelia Esposito is an Indologist who earned her MA from the University of Tübingen in 1998 and studied at the University of Heidelberg. She served as an assistant professor of Indology at the University of Würzburg, attested 2012–2015.

Anna Balikci-Denjongpa is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned her PhD from SOAS University of London under Lionel Caplan in 2002. In 2002, she became Research Coordinator at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology.

Anna Filigenzi is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She lectured at the University of Naples "L'Orientale", directed the Italian Archaeological Mission in Afghanistan in 2003, and held a post at the University of Naples Federico II in 2021.
